candidates.exact_span: The limit for viable helminth ova is less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a numeric helminth-ova limit and whether it is measured before or after pathogen treatment; different readings of the timing and limit basis change which enforceable limit applies and when monitoring must occur.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 4 - The density of enteric viruses in the sewage sludge shall be less than one Plaque- forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a numeric enteric-virus limit and ties it to specific use/disposal or bagged-sale events; interpreting which trigger applies (or whether an event occurred) changes the applicable limit, monitoring obligation, and whether missing results reflect no required monitoring versus unresolved evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The density of viable helminth ova in the sewage sludge shall be less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weigh t basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or dispose d or at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines a separate helminth-ova numeric limit under Alternative 4 with event-based timing; different interpretations of the triggering events or dry-weight basis change limit applicability, required monitoring episodes, and how absent measurements are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 5 - Sewage sludge shall be treated by one of the Processes to Further Reduce Pathogens (PFRP) described in 503 Appendix B. PFRPs include composting, heat drying, heat treatment, and thermophilic aerobic digestion.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Offers a process-based compliance path instead of numeric density limits; whether a facility is evaluated under this alternative changes which monitoring is required and whether missing numeric results reflect conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 6 - Sewage sludge shall be treated by a process that is equivalent to a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides an equivalency-based compliance path contingent on individual EPA approval; interpreting whether approval exists changes applicable monitoring obligations and how missing numeric evidence should be categorized.

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 2 and 3 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Excludes two Class B compliance pathways for Texas permits; misapplying this authorization rule would change which limits and monitoring alternatives are operative and how absent or process-based evidence is interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 1 - Seven random samples of the sewage sludge shall be collected for one monitoring episode at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the sample count, episode structure, and event trigger for Class B Alternative 1 monitoring; different readings of when sludge is used or disposed change whether monitoring was required and whether missing data is a no-obligation period or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The geometric mean of the density of fecal coliform in the samples collected shall be less than either 2,000,000 MPN per gram of total solids (dry weight basis) or 2,000,000 Colony Forming Units per gram of total solids (dry weight basis).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the enforceable Class B fecal-coliform numeric limit, aggregation method (geometric mean), units (MPN vs CFU), and dry-weight basis; interpreting any of these differently changes limit applicability and exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 2 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in one of the Processes to significantly Reduce Pathogens described in 503 Appendix B.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Describes a process-based Class B compliance alternative; whether it is available (given the Texas authorization restriction) affects required monitoring and whether lack of numeric fecal-coliform results reflects a non-numeric compliance path or missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Alternative 3 - Sewage sludge shall be treated in a process that is equivalent to a PSRP, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides an equivalency-based Class B compliance path contingent on individual approval; interpreting approval status and Texas authorization changes monitoring obligations and missing-evidence classification.
